label: Four CLI entrypoints tearing the process down before stdio drains

origin.note: Built for the OAI-221 overnight tuning matrix, 2026-08-26 — never scored by any run before this corpus. process.exit() tears the process down before Node drains queued stdio writes, truncating a large payload at the pipe buffer. Fixed at four sibling sites by replacing process.exit(n) with process.exitCode = n.

defects.description: The UserError catch calls process.exit(1) after writing to stderr, and falls through to an unconditional throw with no return — a large error message can be truncated at the pipe buffer before the process dies.
Same class: process.exit(1) immediately after writing the error and hint to stderr.
Same class in the catch handler for main(argv).
The success path exits with the resolved code immediately, same truncation hazard as the three error-path sites.

dropped.claim: ttl-challenge.mjs's catch-branch process.exit(1) at line 235 is a fifth site.
dropped.reason: Same file and same fix as exit-truncates-ttl-challenge; an anchor match on 'process.exit(1)' cannot distinguish the two calls in this file, so only the .then() site is scored to avoid crediting one finding twice.
